name: Azerbaijan
summary_text: Azerbaijan is dangerous for trans visitors. The documented pattern is grim: a trans woman was tortured and murdered in Baku in July 2023; a second trans woman's murder in March 2024 was met with a police response lacking comprehensive investigation; several other trans people were physically assaulted, including by police themselves; and two trans women were detained for “hooliganism” for making noise. Government-affiliated media air targeted discriminatory hate speech. Trans people face total economic marginalisation (black-market work, precarious housing). Nothing formally criminalises gender expression, but police are perpetrators rather than protectors, and the state is one of the world's more closed authoritarian systems — there is no recourse and no community infrastructure that can operate openly. An April 2024 ECtHR ruling found violations in Azerbaijan's treatment of LGBTI applicants. For a visitor: no statute bars entry or expression, but discovery risks police abuse with no remedy, and the murder-impunity pattern is documented.

sources.claim_summary: ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2025 (covering 2024) chapter on Azerbaijan. Documents the March murder of a trans woman in Baku met with an inadequate police investigation; state-affiliated Real TV airing discriminatory hate speech against LGBTI people after a Women's Day march demanding trans healthcare access; a family forcibly transporting an 18-year-old woman to Baku after she came out; and an April ECtHR ruling on the September 2017 police arrests and mistreatment of LGBTI people, which Azerbaijan acknowledged in 2019.

ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2024 (covering 2023) chapter on Azerbaijan. Documents a July police raid on a private birthday party where queer guests were subjected to forced medical examinations, physical and sexual harassment, and threats of outing; QueeRadar monitoring found 77% of 428 analysed media pieces hateful or biased against LGBTIQ people; and an activist being told to remove a rainbow flag in a Baku cafe.

sources.title: No job, no flat: trans people in the margins in Azerbaijan
sources.claim_summary: OC Media feature by Ali Malikov on trans people in Azerbaijan: discrimination has direct economic impacts - trans people are rejected from jobs and housing, pushed into black-market work and precarious housing. Profiles 'Durdana', 29, arrested, denied housing and employment, and dependent on community support after her trans-friendly employer shut down.

sources.title: Azerbaijan: Anti-Gay Crackdown | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: HRW (Oct 2017): Azerbaijan's anti-gay crackdown - police raids in Baku in September 2017 detained dozens of LGBT people on bogus charges, with beatings and forced medical examinations documented; HRW called for investigation and release.

Gender & Development Social Union shadow report to CEDAW (44th session) on discrimination and violence against lesbian, bisexual and transgender people in Azerbaijan: documents state-approved ignorance, employment discrimination, militant homophobia/transphobia in official and private media, forced marriages, and the impossibility of changing identity documents for trans women; the organisation serves 200+ LBT people.

sources.title: Outcry as Azerbaijan police launch crackdown on LGBT community | Azerbaijan | The Guardian
sources.claim_summary: The Guardian (Sept 2017): outcry as Azerbaijan police launch crackdown on the LGBT community - at least 60 people imprisoned or fined after raids in the capital; part of a wave of arrests ahead of the Islamic Solidarity Games.

sources.title: Azerbaijan: Pop Music vs. Islam | Eurasianet
sources.claim_summary: EurasiaNet (May 2012): Azerbaijani pop music vs Islamic fundamentalism - Iranian clerics demanded Baku cancel Eurovision 2012 and any 'gay pride', calling it a 'Zionist and gay festival'; a senior presidential official responded that Azerbaijan would not host a gay parade - context of regional pressure on LGBT visibility.
